bib.title: In-Context Learning with Long-Context Models: An In-Depth Exploration

legacy_report:
SOURCE: In-Context Learning with Long-Context Models: An In-Depth Exploration. Bertsch, Ivgi, Xiao, Alon, Berant, Gormley, Neubig (CMU, Tel Aviv). arXiv:2405.00200v2 [cs.CL], 3 Mar 2025. The extraction names no venue, so treat it as a preprint.

COVERAGE: All 31 pages and all 91,025 chars were read, including the appendices (saturation, copying test, finetuning details, attention-mask ablation, prompt formats). The reference list was skimmed, and the dataset prompt examples in G.x were only partly read. Page numbers below are approximate, taken from section order.

CLAIMS (ranked)
- Accuracy keeps rising with many-shot ICL on large-label-space classification, far past the 4k window.
  number: up to 50.8 points from 10 to 1000 demos; average 36.8 across 5 datasets.
  setup: Llama2-7b-80k (Fu et al. 2024), 5 classification datasets, random demos, constrained decoding, 250-example test subsample.
  quote: "Scaling up from 10 to 1000 demonstrations results in accuracy gains of up to 50.8 points (and an average of 36.8 points across 5 datasets for Llama2-80k)."
  where: §3.2, p.3
- Retrieval ICL beats random demos at short context, but the gap shrinks as demos grow.
  number: Banking-77 BM25 gain falls from 51.5 points (1-shot) to 4.9 points (1500-shot).
  setup: Llama2 variants on Banking-77, BM25 retrieval vs random selection.
  quote: "On Banking-77, the dataset where retrieval is most beneficial, the performance gain from BM25 retrieval drops from 51.5 points at 1-shot ICL to 4.9 points at 1500-shot ICL."
  where: §3.2, p.4
- A single cached random demo set costs little at long context.
  number: penalty never more than 5 points, as low as 1.8 points (2000-shot, TREC).
  setup: the longest contexts tested, 7B models.
  quote: "the performance penalty for doing so is never more than 5 points, and as low as 1.8 points (in 2000-shot ICL on TREC)."
  where: §3.2, p.4
- BM25 and BERTScore-Recall retrievers differ at small k and become nearly identical at large k. Neither wins everywhere: BSR is better on TREC, BM25 on Banking-77.
  number: none
  quote: "the performance difference between the two retrieval methods diminishes with larger k, so that BM25 and BSR have nearly identical performance at long-context ICL."
  where: §3.2, p.4, Fig 2
- Example order matters less at long context.
  number: under half as many labels flip at 1000-shot as at 10-shot.
  setup: % of predictions that change under random reshuffle, averaged over 3 shuffles, 5 datasets.
  quote: "Across all datasets, the percent of labels flipped by shuffling in 1000-shot ICL is less than half the percentage flipped in 10-shot ICL."
  where: §4, p.5, Fig 4
- Grouping same-label examples hurts more as the context grows.
  number: -25.7 points at 1169-shot.
  setup: Llama2-32k, Clinic-150, examples sorted by label vs random order.
  quote: "at 1169-shot ICL, label sorting decreases accuracy by 25.7 percentage points."
  where: §4, p.5, Fig 5
- Using the full context is not harmful. Accuracy is near-monotone, with no significant drop at higher counts.
  number: none
  quote: "it is minimally not harmful to performance."
  where: §4, p.4-5
- ICL beats LoRA with few examples. Full finetuning on far more data than fits in context wins on most datasets.
  number: none
  setup: Llama2-7b with classification head, finetuned 30 epochs; test-set checkpoint selection, which favours finetuning.
  quote: "for most datasets, LoRA finetuning performance never exceeds long-context ICL performance even with additional examples (e.g. Figure 3a); however, for most datasets, full finetuning with drastically more examples than fit in-context yields the highest performance."
  where: §3.3, p.4-5
- On Clinic-150 (the most labels), finetuning never beats ICL at the same number of examples.
  number: none
  quote: "on the dataset with the most labels, Clinic-150, neither LoRA finetuning nor full finetuning ever outperforms ICL at the same number of examples."
  where: §3.3, p.5
- Finetuning offers cheaper inference at similar performance.
  number: 4096 finetuning examples vs 1000 prompted examples.
  quote: "finetuning on 4096 examples may still be preferable to prompting with 1000 if efficiency of inference is a major priority."
  where: §3.3, p.5
- Frontier models saturate early on intent classification, and part of the gain is fewer invalid labels.
  number: 50 to 3000 demos.
  setup: Claude Sonnet 3.5 and Llama 3.1 405B on Clinic-150, no constrained decoding, a single run.
  quote: "there may be diminishing returns on relatively simple tasks such as intent classification at even the 1,000-example scale."
  where: §4, p.6, Fig 6
- The gain comes from retrieval-like use of many demos, not from cross-demo contextualization. Blockwise attention between demos recovers most of full-attention accuracy.
  number: a block of 50 examples recovers 95% of full attention (Banking-77). Block sizes below 10 give near-zero accuracy.
  setup: Llama2-32k, with an attention sink block plus two local blocks; the test example attends to everything.
  quote: "95% of the performance of full attention is recovered by a block of 50 examples in the case of Banking-77"
  where: §5, p.7, Fig 8-9
- Attention-mask ablation (Banking-77, Llama2-80k, b=50, 500 demos).
  number: full causal 80.04; local block only 18.72; sink+2 local blocks 77.51; sink only 62.15; 1 local block 51.16; sink+1 local 75.12.
  quote: "Figure 17f 50 1 2 77.51"
  where: Appx F, Table 6
- Saturation point (95% of max accuracy) comes later for bigger label spaces.
  number: Clinic-150 on Llama2-80k saturates at 1000 demos (max fit 2000). TREC saturates at 75.
  quote: "Clinic-150 - (145) 750 (1169) 1000 (2000) 750 (1212)"
  where: Appx A, Table 3
  Halving the label space reduces the saturation point, but not by half.
- Long-context ICL also works for generation, with caveats.
  number: gains up to at least 250-shot.
  setup: SAMSum summarization, BERTScore; retrieval sometimes underperforms random.
  quote: "we observe increased performance with additional demonstrations up to at least 250-shot ICL."
  where: §3.2
- Long-context models are about as good as their base at short context, with some regression.
  number: none
  quote: "We observe degradation in performance in some settings for Llama2-32k"
  where: Appx B
- Models do not copy labels perfectly for examples they have seen in-context.
  number: 80-100% (e.g. Llama2-32k 80.0 at 1 shot, 98.9 at 250 shots).
  setup: Banking-77 and Clinic-150 averaged; test examples are the same ones placed in-context.
  quote: "no model is able to uniformly copy correctly from the input."
  where: Appx B, Table 5
- Constrained decoding raises accuracy, mostly on high-label-space datasets, but trends hold without it.
  number: none
  quote: "while performance is lower, especially in the higher-label-space datasets, the general trends hold."
  where: Appx D

Table 2 (best / at-max accuracy, random selection): Qwen2.5 TREC 94.68/94.40, Clinic-150 93.16/92.76. Llama2-4k Banking-77 56.36/56.36. The text calls this "Table 6" in places, so the numbering is inconsistent.

LIMITS
- The authors concede (Limitations section): open-source models, mostly the Llama-2 family; no non-LoRA PEFT; mainly classification ("care should be taken in generalizing to new tasks").
- Most models are 7B and not instruction-tuned. Prompts have no instruction or system prompt, only "Question:/Type:" prefixes. Prompt-format effects are not studied.
- Test set is 250 sampled examples per dataset. Finetuning checkpoints were chosen on the test set, which gives finetuning an upper bound.
- Frontier-model evidence is one run per count on one dataset (Clinic-150), without constrained decoding.
- Dated: 2024-era models (Llama-2, Claude 3.5 Sonnet). Nothing on reasoning models or instruction-tuned models with chat templates.
- Many-shot jailbreaking is flagged as a risk (Anil et al. 2024).

BUILDS ON
- Agarwal et al. 2024 (many-shot ICL, concurrent)
- Ratner et al. 2022 (parallel context windows; formatting and constrained decoding)
- Acharya et al. 2024 (Star Attention)
- Xiao et al. 2024 (attention sink)
- Guo et al. 2024 (Block Sparse Attention)
- Fu et al. 2024 (80k Llama)
- Levy et al. 2023 and 2024 (retrieval; context hurting)
- Lu et al. 2022 (order sensitivity)
- Robertson & Zaragoza 2009 (BM25)
- Gupta et al. 2023 (BERTScore-Recall selection)
- Hu et al. 2022 (LoRA)
- Mosbach 2023, Liu 2022 (T-few), Asai 2023 (finetuning vs ICL comparisons)
- Li et al. 2024 (tasks where long context does not help)
- Lin & Lee 2024 (ICL task retrieval vs learning)
- Pan 2023
- Milios 2023

CODE: none. The only snippets are prompt formats in Appendix G, e.g. "Question: ...\nType: description\n==\n" (Fig 19). Constrained decoding adds a large constant to the logits of valid label tokens (Appx D).

FIGURES (not rendered; the captions are in the extraction)
- Fig 1, p.1: accuracy rises with the number of examples up to 80K tokens.
- Fig 2: BM25 vs BSR vs random.
- Fig 3: retrieval ICL, random ICL, PEFT and full finetuning on Clinic-150 and TREC-fine. It shows the ICL vs finetuning crossover.
- Fig 4: % of labels flipped by reordering.
- Fig 5: label sorting penalty.
- Fig 6: Claude and Llama 3.1 405B saturation, with the invalid-label fraction.
- Fig 7: blockwise attention mask.
- Fig 8-9: block size vs full attention.

PROBLEMS: Extraction was clean. There are no embedded instructions. The text refers to the results table as both "Table 2" and "Table 6". Figure images were not inspected, so numbers that appear only in plots are left out. The target note was grep-checked for "bertsch" with no hits, so it does not cite this paper yet. I did not read the note otherwise.
